evals.prompt: The Goal candidate passed review and the black-box verifier yesterday, but the approved budget changed from 4 hours to 90 minutes while a replacement worker updated the same branch. Produce the delivery packet and tell me whether it can be handed off now.
evals.expected_output: The packet preserves the raw request and records the budget lease change as candidate drift; the old reviewer/verifier receipts are invalidated, status is blocked or invalidated, and handoff requires refreeze plus fresh verifier PASS and final reviewer accept.
expectations: Produces a structured delivery packet or packet-shaped artifact preserving raw request, candidate, budget, and receipt identities.
Records both the budget lease change and branch update as drift against the previously reviewed candidate.
Invalidates the old reviewer and verifier receipts and returns blocked or invalidated rather than handoff-ready.
Requires refreeze, a fresh exact-candidate verifier PASS, and final reviewer acceptance before handoff.

evals.prompt: I prepared a changelog-only candidate on local main at 8e7c... from origin/main, but origin/main advanced to a new commit while the release notes were being reviewed. Can we fast-forward and call it delivered? Track the exact refs and next action.
evals.expected_output: The packet records the original base and observed remote movement, blocks the stale fast-forward/delivery claim, and requires refreezing against the new remote base with a new candidate identity and receipts before any release handoff.
expectations: Records the candidate commit, original base, and newly observed remote ref as distinct exact identities without inventing hashes.
Classifies remote movement as base or candidate drift and refuses to call the stale candidate delivered.
Requires integration or transplant onto the new remote base followed by a new frozen candidate identity.
Requires fresh receipts for the refrozen candidate before release handoff rather than treating fast-forward mechanics as proof.

evals.prompt: Six feature branches are ready to merge into a heavily dirty shared main checkout. Two branches touch overlapping files, three unrelated chat files are being edited concurrently, and the index contains user staging. Give me the exact delivery/integration packet and safe sequence for local integration without losing dirty paths or index state.
evals.expected_output: The packet records all six branch refs and dirty/index baselines, starts main-first, escalates to a detached isolated worktree only for the observed conflict/concurrent-write risk, validates the merge tree, performs CAS against expected-old main, never mutates the live index, and proves preservation before a delivered-ref receipt.
expectations: Records all six source refs plus the expected old main ref, dirty-path baseline, and staged-index baseline in a packet or ledger.
Begins with a read-only main-first feasibility check and escalates to an isolated detached worktree because concrete overlap and concurrent-write risks exist.
Validates the integrated tree before updating main and uses a compare-and-swap check against the expected old main ref.
Never mutates the shared checkout live index; any optional index view uses an explicit alternate GIT_INDEX_FILE, and preservation is proved before a delivered-ref receipt.
